Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 48-year-old man with 3-day history of acute watery diarrhoea (5–6/day) preceded by brief vomiting, no blood, minimal appetite, subjective low-grade fever day 1, feeling dehydrated and weak.  
- No abdominal pain, no sick contacts, no suspicious food recall.  
- PMH mild intermittent asthma.  
- Likely diagnosis: self-limiting viral gastroenteritis.  
- Differential includes bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis (moderate likelihood) and, less likely, C. difficile or other causes (see below).  
- No red-flag features (blood in stool, severe pain, persistent fever) at present; telephone safety-netting provided.

Management Plan
- Advise aggressive oral rehydration: water plus oral rehydration salts (Dioralyte) as directed.  
- Paracetamol for fever/weakness – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
- Rest and remain off work until diarrhoea-free for 24–48 h; likely need 1–2 further days off.  
- Monitor for red-flag symptoms (bloody stool, high fever, worsening pain, persistent vomiting); seek review or ED if they occur.  
- Follow-up: If not improved within one week, return for face-to-face review and consider stool studies and blood tests.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Viral gastroenteritis (High): abrupt onset vomiting followed by 3 days watery diarrhoea, self-limited, no blood or severe pain.  
- Bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis (Moderate): similar duration; initial vomiting fits toxin-mediated illness, though lack of abdominal cramps or fever less supportive.  
- Clostridioides difficile infection (Low): watery diarrhoea possible but no recent antibiotics/hospitalization.
